tr.td: Primary care visit one month after right hip fracture repair, with dementia and caregiver assessment
Neurology consultation for Alzheimer's disease staging, medication review, and evening restlessness
Three-month post-fracture visit with bone density testing and zoledronic acid
Six-month post-fracture, dementia, and caregiver review
Stop oxycodone and diphenhydramine, keep acetaminophen scheduled, and finish 35 days of enoxaparin; review every medicine against the AGS Beers Criteria at each visit
Neurology consultation to stage the dementia, review donepezil benefit and its bradycardia and fall risk, and advise on evening restlessness without antipsychotics
Home physical and occupational therapy, a home safety assessment, and a CDC STEADI fall-risk check at every visit
Replete vitamin D, aim for 1,000 to 1,200 mg of calcium a day from food, then obtain DXA and give intravenous zoledronic acid at about three months once calcium and kidney function are checked
Monitor dementia on the CMID schedule: yearly MoCA, FAST stage, and ADL and IADL scores; neuropsychiatric screen and depression screen at follow-up
Support the caregiver: Zarit Burden Interview at the first and six-month visits, weekly respite, a home health aide, caregiver education, and Alzheimer's Association support services
Advance care planning with the patient and spouse: confirm the health care agent, discuss goals of care, and complete a POLST form; revisit at each change in stage
Walk household distances with a walker and supervision, with a Barthel Index of 75 or more, by the three-month visit
Barthel Index rose from 55 to 75; walks in the house and garden with a walker
25-hydroxyvitamin D of 30 ng/mL or more by three months, then the first zoledronic acid infusion
No further falls through the six-month visit
No falls; Timed Up and Go improved from 24 to 16 seconds
Lower the spouse's Zarit Burden Interview score by at least 10 points by six months
Zarit score fell from 41 to 27 with weekly respite, a home health aide, and caregiver education
Document a health care agent, goals of care, and a POLST form by the three-month visit
Health care agent confirmed and POLST completed with the patient and spouse

Neuropsychiatric screen (NPI-Q): evening restlessness and repeated questions, mild; no hallucinations or aggression; Confusion Assessment Method negative for delirium [S]
Alert, pleasant, and sociable; tells familiar stories; oriented to person, not to date; MoCA 11 of 30 [S]
Mood good by his report and his spouse's; GDS-15 below the threshold for depression [S]
